name: Rector’s Palace
description: The Gothic and Renaissance palace where the elected rector of the Republic of Ragusa lived and governed. It now holds the city museum.

name: City Walls and Pile Gate
description: Stone walls nearly two kilometers long around the old town, entered from the west through Pile Gate and topped by the round Minčeta Tower.

name: Old Port
description: The small harbor on the east side of the walled town, where the merchant ships of the old republic once docked.

name: Sponza Palace
description: A 16th-century palace that served as the customs house and mint. It now holds the archives of the old republic.

name: Fort Imperial
description: A fort on Mount Srđ above the city, built by the French in the early 1800s. It was a key defensive point during the 1991–92 siege.

name: Fort Lovrijenac
description: A fortress on a sea cliff outside the western walls, used as a stage for open-air plays in summer.
